test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Electrician) Official Paper (Held On: 02 May, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: If 'P' is the number of poles on a rotor of an alternator, 'n' is the number of revolutions made per second by the rotor, then the frequency will be:
solution:
__**Concept**__

In an alternator:

 
• One pair of poles (2 poles) produces one electrical cycle.
 
• If the rotor has P poles, then it has P/2 pole pairs.
 
• If the rotor speed is n revolutions per second, then each revolution produces P/2 cycles.

Hence, the frequency is:

f={Pover 2}times n
